question.worked_solution:
First, we factor $2{cos}^{2}⁡x$ from the first two terms:

$$
\frac{2{cos}^{4}⁡x+2{cos}^{2}⁡x{sin}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}=\frac{2{cos}^{2}⁡x({cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x)-1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}
$$

Next, we use the Pythagorean identity to rewrite the expression in the parentheses, and then we simplify the resulting expression as much as possible:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2{cos}^{2}⁡x({cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x)-1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} & =\frac{2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{2{cos}^{2}⁡x-({cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{2{cos}^{2}⁡x-{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}-\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & ={cot}^{2}⁡x-1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that:

$$
\frac{2{cos}^{4}⁡x+2{cos}^{2}⁡x{sin}^{2}⁡x-1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}={cot}^{2}⁡x-1
$$
